title: Indra/Minsait is ruled out on both size and posture at 62,396 staff
content:
Indra/Minsait is excluded on size and posture together. The size is recorded precisely — 62,396 people — which places it several orders of magnitude beyond the firms the screen treats as workable first partners. The posture is legible from its stack: Microsoft, SAP, Salesforce, AWS and IBM, a portfolio of proprietary vendor alliances with no open-source anchor.

Either criterion alone would be enough. At this headcount any engagement is an enterprise procurement with a committee, a vendor-management function and an alliance team that scores new technologies against existing partner commitments. And a portfolio built entirely on proprietary alliances means the reference architecture a Powerhouse layer would join is one where client-owned, open infrastructure is not the default.

The note is terse because the verdict needs no nuance: it is not a near miss whose ranking could shift on new evidence, but a structural mismatch on the two attributes the screen weights first.
